headline: Highest risk is medium: Dify can write and egress by default, but LightZero is non-networked and read-only, so pairwise harm is limited to shared-workspace misuse and workflow misrouting.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and run tools, so if LightZero outputs are manually copied into Dify, prompt injection is possible. LightZero itself has no file or network surfaces, so there is no automatic bridge. The pathway exists only through unusual operator bridging, and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator copies LightZero-generated text into a Dify prompt or knowledge file
IF Dify tools are configured to treat imported text as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste template that labels LightZero output as untrusted
Disable automatic ingestion of game logs into Dify prompts
Add a manual review step before any Dify tool call
Keep LightZero outputs in a separate folder from Dify inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs and knowledge-base files, while LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage from LightZero into Dify is not inherent. Any exposure requires operator movement of files or text between them.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are manually pasted into Dify conversations
IF Dify knowledge-base uploads include LightZero logs containing sensitive content
mitigations: Do not paste raw LightZero logs into Dify
Store LightZero artifacts outside Dify-managed workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; LightZero cannot write, modify git, or use the network. Because only one agent has write authority, there is no meaningful concurrent write conflict in the default pair. The remaining risk is limited to operator confusion over shared files, not resource contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by the operator
IF Dify subprocesses and LightZero jobs are scheduled against the same files
mitigations: Avoid sharing git repositories between the agents

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can act on tool outputs and write files, so if LightZero results are copied into Dify, Dify may treat them as authoritative without verification. LightZero is a game-playing system and does not itself verify downstream claims. The interaction is not automatic, but the default Dify workflow tooling makes misrouting plausible.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are used as inputs to a Dify workflow without a validation step
IF Dify is configured to trigger actions from imported text
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before Dify acts on LightZero output
Require structured output with explicit confidence fields
Disable action-taking tools in the Dify workflow
Log provenance for every imported LightZero result

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: Dify is open-source and self-hostable, while LightZero is a local game-playing library with no data classes or egress. The pair does not show PHI, EU PII, residency, or retention conflicts in the provided profiles, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through Dify
IF LightZero is extended to process regulated datasets
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair
Review Dify retention settings before deployment
